title: Prompt Influence Mapping and Quant Sensitivity Matrix
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This document defines a reproducible process and artifact (the Quant Sensitivity Matrix) that maps prompt structure and pragmatic features to observed quality degradation under quantized model variants. It is intended for ML engineers, model stewards, and evaluator owners who must certify prompt families for quant migration or configure quant fallbacks in production.

Goals
- Provide a repeatable evaluation workflow to measure how prompt components (system messages, instruction framing, few-shot examples, delimiters, priming tokens) interact with quantization artifacts.
- Produce a human-readable matrix that classifies sensitivity and prescribes mitigations and runtime fallback policies.
- Standardize thresholds and telemetry needed for automatic gating and canary rollouts.

When to use this playbook
- Prior to promoting quantized model artifacts to staging/dedicated.
- When onboarding customer prompt bundles with long-context or function-call semantics.
- After a regression triage that indicates prompt-shaped failures post-quant migration.

Key concepts
- Prompt component: discrete parts of a prompt (system, instruction, examples, context-window priming).
- Sensitivity score: a normalized 0.0–1.0 number capturing relative degradation vs full-precision baseline for a given metric (higher = more sensitive).
- Quant Sensitivity Matrix (QSM): table mapping prompt components and workload slices to sensitivity bands (Low/Medium/High) plus prescriptive mitigations.

Artifact: Quant Sensitivity Matrix (QSM)
- Deliverable: QSM CSV and a Confluence/JSON summary for each model-version and quant-config.
- Columns (CSV): prompt_family_id, component, workload_slice, sample_count, baseline_metric, quant_metric, delta_pct, sensitivity_score, band, recommended_action, telemetry_keys, owner, notes

Measurement metrics and thresholds
- Primary fidelity metrics (choose 1–2 per prompt family):
  - Response Stability Index (RSI): n-gram-agnostic similarity + semantic embedding cosine anchored to baseline; reported 0–100.
  - Functional correctness: binary/score for function-call success, slot-filling, or API-construction tests.
  - Safety / guardrail pass rate: percent of probes flagged by safety sentinels.
- Acceptance thresholds (default):
  - Low sensitivity: delta_pct <= 2% and RSI drop <= 3 points -> band = Low
  - Medium sensitivity: 2% < delta_pct <= 7% or RSI drop between 3–10 points -> band = Medium
  - High sensitivity: delta_pct > 7% or RSI drop > 10 points or functional correctness loss > 1.5% absolute -> band = High
- Operational alerting: any High sensitivity on production probes must trigger regression-oncall per regression triage runbook.

Evaluation workflow (recommended pipeline)
1) Probe cementing and canonicalization
   - Identify representative prompt families and generate a stratified probe set (minimum 500 probes per family for mixed-production workloads; 200 for niche slices).
   - Canonicalize variable placeholders (user names, timestamps) into deterministic anchors to reduce noise.
2) Baseline collection (FP32/FP16 reference)
   - Run probes against the promoted full-precision reference model 3 seeds, capture RSI, functional checks, logits (optionally), token-level timing.
3) Quant sweep (per quant config)
   - Run identical probes against each quant variant (8-bit, 4-bit, QAT results). Use same RNG seeds where applicable.
4) Delta analysis and sensitivity scoring
   - Compute delta_pct for the chosen metric(s) and map to sensitivity_score (linear mapping: 0–1 from 0–20% delta, clamp >20% to 1).
5) QSM generation and review
   - Aggregate per-slice scores into the matrix CSV and upload to artifact registry.
6) Mitigation and rollout decisioning
   - For Low band: allow promotion with standard monitoring.
   - For Medium band: require canary in staging for 24–72h with traffic weighting <5% and elevated telemetry retention.
   - For High band: do not promote; either keep FP variant for that prompt family or schedule targeted quant re-tuning and re-evaluation.

| prompt_family_id | component     | workload_slice         | sample_count | baseline_RSI | quant_RSI | delta_pct | sensitivity_score | band  | recommended_action                     | telemetry_keys                             | owner        |
|------------------|---------------|------------------------|--------------:|-------------:|----------:|----------:|------------------:|:-----:|:---------------------------------------:|:-------------------------------------------:|:------------:|
| retail-returns-01 | few-shot      | long-receipt-detail    | 600          | 92           | 84        | 8.7%      | 0.44             | Medium | Canary (staging), add example simplifier | rsi,func_success,fidelity_bucket           | team-retail  |
| intent-parsing-02 | system        | multi-intent-chained   | 800          | 95           | 93        | 2.1%      | 0.10             | Low    | Promote, monitor minor drift             | rsi,entity_precision                        | team-nlu     |
| code-exec-03      | function-call | multi-tool-codegen     | 500          | 98           | 86        | 12.2%     | 0.61             | High   | Hold promotion; quant retune required    | func_success,token_unrolling,call_exactness | team-codegen |

Prescriptive mitigations (by band)
- Low: increase probe frequency in production (weekly), keep 30d telemetry retention for these keys.
- Medium: apply prompt softening (reduce few-shot examples to 1–2, add explicit delimiters), enable selective FP fallback for that route, and run a 72h canary with A/B fidelity checks.
- High: disallow quant variant for the prompt family in routing policies; open a quant-retune ticket and assign to model-owner. If the route must use quant due to capacity, add automated rephrase path that short-circuits to a verified template.

Runtime controls and routing policies
- Route-key annotation: when registering a prompt family in the Prompt Registry, include qsm_band and qsm_owner tags. Example: {"prompt_family_id":"retail-returns-01","qsm_band":"Medium","qsm_owner":"team-retail"}
- Smart routing rules (examples):
  - If qsm_band == High then route to FP variant or to Dedicated capacity tagged fp-fallback=true.
  - If qsm_band == Medium then sample 1% traffic to quant variant behind canary flag and 99% to baseline for 72h.
  - If RSI_drop > 5 and user_impact==true then escalate automatically.

Instrumentation and telemetry requirements
- Required telemetry keys: rsi, embedding_cosine_to_baseline, func_success, safety_flags, token_loss_per_step, latency_p50/95/99, model_variant, prompt_family_id, request_id, seed
- Sampling: probe-derived telemetry for QSM must include full trace for 100% of canary requests; aggregated probes can be sampled at 10% in production after promotion.
- Alert thresholds (default):
  - RSI drop > 6 points sustained over 1000 requests -> P1 alert to ML-oncall.
  - func_success drop > 1% absolute for 10k requests -> P0 and automatic rollback.

Canary and rollout checklist
1) Confirm QSM generated and reviewed by owner and two reviewers.
2) Build ephemeral canary cluster with quant variant and instrument full telemetry retention for the route.
3) Run synthetic probe flood (10k probes/min for 15m) and verify no functional regressions.
4) Start 24–72h traffic canary: initial 0.5% traffic, double every 6–12h while monitoring RSI and func_success.
5) If no alerts and metrics within Medium band bounds, continue to 5% for 48h then to standard rollout.
6) If RSI drift observed > alert thresholds, abort and rollback to FP; file regression triage ticket referencing QSM row.

Developer tools and sample commands
- Generate probe set (internal CLI):
  - rw-probe generate --prompt-family retail-returns-01 --strata long-receipt-detail --count 600 --normalize-placeholders --out probes/retail-returns-01-600.json
- Run baseline and quant sweep:
  - rw-eval run --model x-large-fp32 --probes probes/retail-returns-01-600.json --out baseline/retail-returns-01.csv
  - rw-eval run --model x-large-q4_0 --probes probes/retail-returns-01-600.json --out q4/retail-returns-01.csv --seed 42
- Produce QSM (aggregation script):
  - python tools/qsm_aggregator.py --baseline baseline/retail-returns-01.csv --variants q4/retail-returns-01.csv --out qsm/retail-returns-01-qsm.csv

Decision log and ownership
- Default owner for QSM generation: evaluator-owner for the prompt_family (field in Prompt Registry). Team must review QSM within 7 business days of artifact publication.
- If model owner disagrees with banding, they must attach empirical re-run notes and reassign for a second review.

Escalation and regression triage linkages
- Any High band entry that appears in production telemetry should create an automated incident via the regression triage pipeline: label = quant-sensitivity-high, attach QSM CSV row, include probe sample ids. Follow the regression-triage/runbook steps for root cause and rollback.

Appendix A: Example JSON QSM row (single-line)
{"prompt_family_id": "retail-returns-01", "component": "few-shot", "workload_slice": "long-receipt-detail", "sample_count": "600", "baseline_RSI": "92", "quant_RSI": "84", "delta_pct": "8.7", "sensitivity_score": "0.44", "band": "Medium", "recommended_action": "Canary in staging; add example simplifier", "telemetry_keys": "rsi,func_success,fidelity_bucket", "owner": "team-retail"}

Appendix B: Quick tuning recipes for Medium/High slices
- Soft prompt rewriting: remove optional context blocks, use explicit delimiters ("```"), replace multi-example chains with a single canonical example.
- Contrastive anchor priming: add a single example of the desired output shape before user content to stabilize tokenization/attention.
- Loss-smoothing retrain: if available, run a 1–2 epoch targeted QAT pass on a 5–10k probe subset emphasizing the failing slice.

Appendix C: Frequently asked questions
Q: How is RSI computed?
A: RSI is a composite score combining embedding cosine to baseline (weighted 0.6), normalized answer-token overlap (0.25), and function-call exactness (0.15) — scaled to 0–100. Implementation reference: internal library eval.metrics.response_stability_index().

Q: What if a customer prompt family mixes sensitive and insensitive slices?
A: Split the family into deterministic slices and treat each row separately in the QSM. Routing rules operate at route/prompt-family-slice granularity.
